title: Rabbi Zavdi, Son-in-Law of Rabbi Levi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:8: he asked, “Without this is it not forbidden?” Rabbi Yose said: “Explain it,” etc. In Ruth Rabbah 2:10: “Rabbi Chunya, Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Avin, and Rabbi Zavda, son-in-law of Rabbi Levi: The Merciful One never punishes lives first.” In Vayikra Rabbah 17:4 the statement reads “Rav Huna in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua bar Avin and Rabbi Zavdiya, son-in-law of Rabbi Levi, in the name of Rabbi Levi.” In Midrash Shmuel 2:3: “Rabbi Zavdiya, son-in-law of Rabbi Levi, in the name of Rabbi Levi: Like a person who calls a blind man ‘one of abundant light.’” The source is Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1, and there it is Rabbi Zekharyah, son-in-law of Rabbi Levi; see the entry Rabbi Zekharyah.

notes.text: Saved Torat Emet Vayikra Rabbah17:4 fully writes Rav Huna and has Zekharyah, son-in-law of Levi, against the supplied Zavdiya form. All Zavdi/Zavda/Zekharyah witnesses remain distinct. Kilayim1:8 is Jerusalem Talmud.

The consulted Ruth Rabbah 2:10 directly names Zavda, son-in-law of Levi; Vayikra Rabbah 17:4 and Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:8 instead name Zekharyah. The Vayikra witness fully writes Rav Huna. Hyman’s Zavdi/Zavda/Zavdiya/Zekharyah comparisons remain occurrence-specific; no automatic name merger is made.
